description:
VERIFIED: fz says false, Elixir says true.

Elixir's == compares numbers across integer/float; === is the strict form. fz has
only the strict behaviour and no === operator at all (lexer rejects it -- 'a === b'
mis-parses as '(a == b) = ...' with no diagnostic).

Blast radius inside fz-5xp: Enum.member?/2, Enum.uniq, Enum.dedup, List.delete,
List.subtract, and map key identity.

Decide and document: adopt Elixir's ==/=== split, or keep strict-only as a deliberate
divergence. Either way it must be written down -- right now it is neither.

comments.text: Superseded in approach by fz-5xp.18: the ==/!= integer-float and float-integer clauses land as part of the one typed-clause family fix across all six comparison operators, not as a separate change.

title: == behaves as ===: 1 == 1.0 is false
